questions.a: To continue their species by producing new individuals similar to themselves.

questions.q: What is the difference between asexual and sexual reproduction?
questions.a: Asexual needs one parent and makes copies; sexual reproduction uses two parents and produces variation.

questions.q: Why is variation useful to a species?
questions.a: It helps populations survive changes like disease, heat or drought.

questions.q: Name three modes of asexual reproduction.
questions.a: Binary fission, budding, fragmentation and spore formation.
By binary fission - the cell splits into two equal daughter cells.
Fungi like Rhizopus (bread mould) and ferns and mosses among plants.

concepts.title: Sexual Reproduction in Plants and Animals

questions.a: Transfer of pollen from the anther to the stigma of a flower, by wind, water or insects.
The fusion of a male gamete (sperm) with a female gamete (egg) to form a zygote.

questions.q: How do flowering plants and animals differ in gamete transfer?
questions.a: Plants transfer pollen (male gamete carrier) to the stigma; animals move whole gametes or bodies together.
